details.description: DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct is the instruction-tuned chat variant of DeepSeek's DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite code model, from DeepSeek AI. It is a 16-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 2.4 billion active parameters per forward pass, built by further pretraining an intermediate DeepSeek-V2 checkpoint on 6 trillion additional tokens before instruction tuning, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository. It supports 338 programming languages, up from 86 in the original DeepSeek-Coder, and a 128,000-token context window per DeepSeek's documentation. DeepSeek's repository reports it performing competitively with closed models such as GPT-4 Turbo on coding and math benchmarks, at a fraction of the parameter count of DeepSeek-Coder-V2's full 236-billion-parameter version.
advantages: Scores 81.1% on HumanEval, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository.
Scores 68.8% on MBPP+, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository.
Scores 86.4% on GSM8K, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository.
Supports 338 programming languages, expanded from 86 in the original DeepSeek-Coder, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository.
Uses a sparse Mixture-of-Experts architecture with only 2.4 billion active parameters out of 16 billion total, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
disadvantages: Scores 0 out of 30 on AIME 2024, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository.
A smaller, lower-capacity variant of the 236-billion-parameter full DeepSeek-Coder-V2 model, per DeepSeek's GitHub repository.
use_cases: Code generation and completion across 338 programming languages.
General-purpose instruction-following chat with a 128,000-token context window.

sources.title: DeepSeek Coder V2 Lite Instruct - Fireworks AI

notes: Catalog's max_input_tokens and max_output_tokens (163,840, identical for both) exceed DeepSeek's documented native context of 128,000 tokens; Fireworks' own page for this model also lists 163k in its specification section alongside a 128K headline figure. Kept catalog's values per instructions. LiveCodeBench score (24.3) is reported by DeepSeek without stating pass@1 vs pass@5; treated as an accuracy-style percentage consistent with the other benchmarks in the same table.
